source: Written by Claude (claude-opus-5-5) from the county counts (AP via The New York Times), the 2024 baseline and Census ACS 2023 context.

55009.t:
Brown County flipped in the race for Wisconsin governor. Trump carried it by 8 points in 2024, and Democrat Crowley won it by 2 points over Republican Tiffany, 58,410 votes to 55,947. That 10-point move toward the Democrats was slightly larger than the state's 9-point shift and ranked 13th of Wisconsin's 72 counties. It was one of seven Trump counties to go Democratic. Similar counties moved alike: Racine shifted 8 points and also flipped, Kenosha moved 12, and Outagamie moved 10 but stayed narrowly Republican.

Turnout fell to 77% of the 2024 vote, from 148,960 ballots to 114,357, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

55097.t:
Portage County moved 11 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor, going from a 1-point Harris edge in 2024 to a 12-point win for Crowley over Tiffany, 19,295 votes to 15,099. That ranks sixth among Wisconsin's 72 counties, ahead of the typical county's 6-point shift and the state's 9-point swing, though below the national typical move of 14. Similar counties shifted less: Sauk by 8, Green by 8, Door by 3.

About 34,394 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Washburn moved further left than similar counties nearby: Marquette, Burnett and Adams each shifted 2 to 3 points. About 8,814 votes were cast, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

Oconto County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but moved 5 points toward the Democrats. That shift was close to Wisconsin's typical county move of 6 points and well below the state's 9-point swing, which carried Crowley to an 8-point statewide win. Neighboring comparisons moved similarly: Marinette by 6, Shawano by 6 and Clark by 5.

Only 18,861 votes were cast, 76% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell whether the move came from voters changing their minds or from some voters staying home.

55105.t:
Rock County voted for Crowley over Tiffany for governor by about 18 points, 39,549 to 27,724. In 2024 it backed Harris by about 7 points, so the county moved 10 points toward the Democrats. That is more than the state's 9-point swing and the typical Wisconsin county's 6, and it ranks ninth of 72 in the state. Similar counties moved about as much: La Crosse 12, Eau Claire 13 and Douglas 11.

Turnout fell to 67,273 votes, 76% of the 2024 total of 88,113. With that drop, the count cannot tell how much of the move came from voters changing their minds and how much from people who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the figures are close to final.

55033.t:
Dunn County stayed Republican in the race for Wisconsin governor but by much less than in 2024. Tiffany beat Crowley 10,561 to 9,188, a margin of 7 points, down from Trump's 16-point win over Harris. That 9-point shift toward the Democrats matches the statewide swing that carried Crowley to an 8-point victory, ranks 16th of Wisconsin's 72 counties, and beats the typical county's 6 points. Among similar counties, Pierce moved 7 points, Oneida 3, and Grant 11.

Turnout fell sharply. About 19,749 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot show how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from Republican-leaning voters staying home.

55078.t:
In the race for Wisconsin governor, Menominee County voted for Crowley over Tiffany 931 to 248, a Democratic margin of 58 points. That is 4 points less Democratic than Harris's 62-point margin in 2024. It was the only one of Wisconsin's 72 counties to move toward the Republicans, while the state as a whole moved 9 points toward the Democrats as Crowley won by 8. Other strongly Democratic counties went the other way: Dane moved 9 points left, Milwaukee 14 and Bayfield 8.

Menominee cast the fewest votes of any county in the state, and turnout fell to 1,179, three-quarters of its 2024 total. The count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55117.t:
Sheboygan County backed Tiffany, the Republican, over Crowley in the race for governor, 28,640 votes to 23,299, a 10-point margin. Trump carried it by 16 points in 2024, so the county moved 6 points toward the Democrats. That matches the typical Wisconsin county's shift of about 6 points but trails the statewide swing of 9, which helped Crowley win by 8. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

Turnout was 51,939 votes, 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among counties of similar size and 2024 vote, Jefferson moved 7 points, while Marathon and St. Croix each moved 5. All three, like Sheboygan, stayed Republican.

55075.t:
Marinette County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but moved about 6 points toward the Democrats. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley there by 32 points, 11,747 votes to 6,024, after Donald Trump carried it by 38 in 2024. That shift matched the typical Wisconsin county, where 71 of 72 moved left, and fell short of the state's 9-point swing as Crowley won statewide by 8. Similar counties moved alike: Shawano by 6 points, Clark and Rusk by 5 each.

Turnout fell sharply: 17,771 votes were cast, 73% of the 2024 total of 24,364. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55057.t:
In the race for Wisconsin governor, Juneau County stayed firmly Republican but by less than in 2024. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley 6,645 to 4,099, a margin of 24 points, down from Donald Trump's 32-point win over Kamala Harris. That 8-point shift toward the Democrats ranks 18th of Wisconsin's 72 counties and is larger than the typical county's 6 points, though close to the statewide swing of 9 points and well short of the 14-point typical move nationally.

Only 10,744 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Similar counties moved less: Kewaunee 5 points, Price 4, Burnett 2.

55119.t:
Taylor County stayed firmly Republican in the race for governor, giving Tiffany 6,005 votes to Crowley's 2,268, a 45-point margin. That is 3 points less Republican than Trump's 48-point win here in 2024. Wisconsin as a whole moved 9 points toward the Democrats, and Crowley won statewide by 8. Taylor's shift ranked 64th of the state's 72 counties and was smaller than in similar counties such as Florence, Clark and Oconto, which each moved about 5 points.

Turnout fell sharply: 8,273 votes were cast, 74% of the 11,172 in 2024. With that many fewer voters, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55109.t:
St. Croix County stayed Republican in the race for governor but by less than in 2024. Tiffany beat Crowley here 26,975 to 20,212, a margin of 14 points, down from Trump's 19-point win over Harris. That 5-point shift toward the Democrats trails the statewide swing of 9 points and is a little below the typical Wisconsin county's 6, ranking 47th of 72. Similar counties moved a bit more: Marathon 5 points, Wood 6 and Walworth 8.

Only 47,187 votes were cast, 78% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot show how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from those who stayed home.

55127.t: Walworth County stayed Republican in the governor's race but by a much smaller margin. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley here 26,405 to 19,856, a 14-point margin, down from Trump's 22-point win in 2024. That 8-point shift toward the Democrats is slightly less than the statewide move of 9 points but larger than the typical Wisconsin county's 6. It ranks 25th of 72 counties, and it moved further than the comparable Republican counties of Manitowoc, Chippewa and St. Croix. Turnout was 46,261, about 77% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally the typical county moved 14 points left.

55081.t:
Monroe County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race but by less than in 2024. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley 10,459 to 7,172, a margin of 19 points, down from Donald Trump's 26-point win over Kamala Harris. That 8-point move toward the Democrats is close to the statewide shift of 9 points and above the typical Wisconsin county's 6, though below the typical national move of 14. Similar Republican counties moved less: Lincoln and Adams by 3 points each, Barron by 4.

Turnout fell sharply, with 17,631 votes cast against 23,321 in 2024, about 76% as many. The count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

55021.t:
Columbia County flipped in the race for governor. Trump carried it by 5 points in 2024; this time Democrat Crowley beat Republican Tiffany by 3, 13,970 votes to 13,174, with 99% of the expected vote counted. That is a 7-point move toward the Democrats, slightly less than the state's 9-point shift and a little more than the typical Wisconsin county's 6. It was one of seven counties in the state to go from Trump to the Democrat.

Turnout was 78% of the 2024 total, 27,144 votes against 34,843, so the count cannot tell voters who switched sides from those who stayed home. Similar counties moved further: Sauk 8 points, Winnebago 10 and Kenosha 12.

55089.t:
Ozaukee County stayed Republican in the race for Wisconsin governor but by less than in 2024. Tom Tiffany (R) beat David Crowley (D) here 26,708 to 24,119, a margin of about 5 points, against Trump's lead of nearly 11 over Harris. That is a move of 5 points toward the Democrats, a little under the typical Wisconsin county's 6 and well short of the state's 9-point swing that gave Crowley an 8-point win. Similar counties moved further: Sheboygan by 6, Outagamie by 10 and Kenosha by 12.

Turnout was 50,827, about 80% of the 2024 vote, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

55031.t:
Douglas County moved about 11 points toward the Democrats in the race for governor. Harris carried it by 5 points in 2024; Crowley won it by 16 over Tiffany, 11,181 votes to 8,070, with 99% of the expected vote counted. That shift is larger than Wisconsin's statewide move of 9 points and ranks eighth of the state's 72 counties, where the typical county moved 6. It also moved more than similar counties nearby: Door shifted 3, Iowa 8 and Ashland 10. Nationally, the typical county moved 14.

About 19,251 votes were cast, roughly three-quarters of the 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot show whether voters changed their minds or Republican-leaning voters stayed home.

55029.t:
Door County moved toward the Democrats in the governor's race, but by less than most of Wisconsin. Crowley beat Tiffany here 9,255 to 8,312, a margin of about 5 points, up from Harris's 2-point edge in 2024. That 3-point shift ranks 63rd of 72 counties. The typical Wisconsin county moved about 6 points left, the state as a whole about 9, and the typical county nationally about 14.

Similar counties moved further: Green by 8 points, and Douglas and Portage by 11 each. Turnout here was 84% of the 2024 vote, with 17,567 ballots against 20,896, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55067.t:
In the race for Wisconsin governor, Tiffany carried Langlade County over Crowley by 31 points, 5,798 votes to 3,033. That is 3 points narrower than Trump's 35-point margin here in 2024, a smaller shift toward the Democrats than in most of the state. Langlade ranks 61st of 72 Wisconsin counties by move, against 6 points for the typical county and a statewide swing of 9. Similar Republican counties moved about as little, from 3 points in Waushara to 5 in Kewaunee.

Turnout fell to 8,831 votes, 76% of the 11,659 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

55093.t:
In the governor's race, Pierce County stayed Republican but by less than it did for president. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley 10,854 to 8,888, a margin of 10 points, after Donald Trump carried the county by 17 in 2024. That 7-point shift toward the Democrats is slightly larger than the typical Wisconsin county's 6 points and smaller than the state's overall 9-point swing, as Crowley won statewide by 8.

Turnout fell sharply: 19,742 votes, 78% of the 2024 total. That means the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Among similar counties, Pierce moved less than Grant (11 points) and Dunn (9) but more than Oneida (3).

55065.t:
In the Wisconsin governor's race, Lafayette County voted for Tom Tiffany (R) over David Crowley (D), 3,691 to 2,847, a Republican margin of 13 points. Trump carried it by 20 in 2024, so the county moved 7 points toward the Democrats. That is a bit more than the typical Wisconsin county (+6) but less than the state as a whole (+9), and well short of the typical national move (+14). Similar counties were mixed: Jackson moved 8 points, Trempealeau 10 and Sawyer 5.

Turnout was 6,538 votes, 74% of the 8,832 cast in 2024, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. With 99% of the expected vote counted, the result is unlikely to shift much.

55013.t:
In the race for Wisconsin governor, Republican Tiffany carried Burnett County over Democrat Crowley 5,552 to 3,055, a margin of 29 points. That is 2 points narrower than Trump's 31-point win here in 2024, one of the smallest shifts in the state: Burnett ranks 70th of 72 counties by move, while the typical Wisconsin county moved 6 points toward the Democrats and the state as a whole moved 9. Similar counties moved somewhat more, from 2 points in Marquette to 5 in Buffalo.

Turnout fell to 8,607 votes, 80% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home. Nationally, the typical county moved 14 points left.

55071.t:
Manitowoc County voted for Tom Tiffany (R) over David Crowley (D) in the governor's race, 20,232 to 14,078, a margin of 18 points. That is 5 points toward the Democrats from Trump's 23-point win in 2024, close to the typical Wisconsin county's 6-point shift and smaller than the state's 9-point swing. It ranks 39th of 72 counties by move. Comparable counties moved somewhat more: Chippewa and Walworth by 8 points each and Wood by 6.

Only 34,310 votes were cast, 74% of the 2024 total. With turnout that much lower, the count cannot show how much of the shift came from voters changing their minds and how much from Republican-leaning voters staying home.

55121.t:
Trempealeau County stayed Republican in the race for Wisconsin governor, but by a much smaller margin. Tom Tiffany beat David Crowley here 6,879 to 5,466, an 11-point Republican margin, down from Donald Trump's 21-point win in 2024. That 10-point shift toward the Democrats ranks 10th among Wisconsin's 72 counties, ahead of the typical county's 6 points and Crowley's 9-point statewide gain, though below the 14-point national typical move. Similar counties split: Jackson moved 8 points and Lafayette 7, while Vilas barely moved.

Turnout fell sharply. Only 12,345 votes were cast, 77% of the 2024 total of 16,066, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55053.t:
In the race for governor, Jackson County voted for Republican Tom Tiffany over Democrat David Crowley, 4,632 to 3,700, a margin of 11 points. Donald Trump carried it by nearly 20 in 2024, so the county moved 8 points toward the Democrats. That is more than the typical Wisconsin county's 6-point shift and close to the state's 9-point swing, but well short of the typical national move of 14. Jackson ranks 22nd of 72 Wisconsin counties by move. Similar counties shifted by comparable amounts: Lafayette 7 points, Sawyer 5 and Trempealeau 10.

The county cast 8,332 votes, 79% of its 2024 total. With that drop in turnout, the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home.

55131.t:
Washington County stayed firmly Republican in the governor's race, backing Tiffany over Crowley 47,165 to 23,559, a margin of about 33 points. In 2024 Trump carried it by 36, so the county moved 3 points toward the Democrats, well short of the 9-point shift statewide that gave Crowley an 8-point win.

Nearly every Wisconsin county moved left, the typical one by 6 points, and Washington ranks 65th of 72. Counties with a similar 2024 vote moved further: Shawano and Marinette by 6 points and Dodge by 5. Turnout was 78% of the 2024 vote, about 70,700 ballots against 91,162, so the count cannot separate voters who changed their minds from those who stayed home.

55095.t:
In the race for Wisconsin governor, Polk County voted for Tiffany over Crowley by 26 points, 13,609 to 8,031. That is 5 points less Republican than its 31-point margin for Trump over Harris in 2024. The shift was smaller than Wisconsin's 9-point swing toward the Democrats, which carried Crowley to a statewide win, and close to the typical Wisconsin county's move of about 6 points. Polk ranks 43rd of 72 counties by move.

Turnout fell sharply. The 21,640 votes cast were 77% of the 2024 total, so the count cannot tell who changed their mind from who stayed home. Among similar counties, Barron moved 4 points, Waupaca 6 and Burnett 2.
